False friends for English speakers

Italian and English share thousands of words from Latin, so it's easy to let your guard down. These words don't mean what you think.

ItalianMeansNot
i parentirelativesparents (i genitori)
la fattoriathe farmthe factory (la fabbrica)
guardareto look at, to watchto guard (sorvegliare)
caldohotcold (freddo)
la camerathe bedroom, the roomthe camera (la macchina fotografica)
la firmathe signaturethe firm (l'azienda)
la cantinathe cellarthe canteen (la mensa)
morbidosoftmorbid (morboso)
la libreriathe bookstorethe library (la biblioteca)
annoiatoboredannoyed (infastidito)
il magazzinothe warehouse, the storeroomthe magazine (la rivista)

The C on an Italian faucet stands for caldo: that's the hot water!

", "

Talk like an Italian

You'll hear these expressions ten times a day. They'll take you straight from the textbook to real conversation.

In bocca al lupo! — Crepi!Good luck! (literally “into the wolf's mouth”, a bit like “break a leg”). The answer is “may it die!”, never “grazie”.
Non vedo l'ora di partire.I can't wait to leave.
Meno male!Thank goodness! Phew!
Figurati!Don't mention it, no problem.
Mi raccomando!Please, make sure you do! Don't forget!
Che ne dici?What do you say? How about it?
Ce l'ho fatta!I did it! I made it!
Non ne posso più.I can't take it anymore.
Fare due passi.To go for a little walk, a stroll.
Dai! / Boh.Come on! / No idea.

The exercises that follow mix these new expressions with everything you've seen since Torino.
